About

Analytics in service of students & decisions

I’m a data analytics professional with 7+ years turning data into decisions across fintech, automotive data, government IT, consulting, and higher-education institutional research.

At UNCW’s Office of Institutional Research & Planning, I build institutional reports and dashboards, strengthen data quality, and partner with campus stakeholders — working day to day with SQL, Python, Tableau, and statistical analysis.

Alongside my role, I’m pursuing a Doctor of Information Technology at Trine University (4.0 GPA), where my interests sit at the intersection of data science, cybersecurity, and responsible, decision-ready analytics. I enjoy connecting with fellow data and analytics professionals — feel free to reach out.

Off the clock, I’m a traveler — I’ve lived in 12 cities across three countries, and I keep a map of all of it.

What AI did today

AI is moving stupid fast, and nobody can keep up by scrolling all day — so I keep a radar. Here’s the short version: what’s new, what to watch out for, and what genuinely blew my mind. Every source competes on merit — the big labs, the startups, the open-source world, all of it.

ai-radar — daily brief / SUN · NOV 08, 2026 · EDITION 022 / The AI Radar — Sunday, November 8, 2026 FEED SYNCED LATEST BRIEF
TL;DR — THE 20-SECOND VERSION An AI just proved a quantum puzzle that stayed unsolved for 18 years, AI agents can finally talk to each other in one shared language, and Claude Code stopped making developers wait — plus an open model retrained to drop propaganda, a huge open model landing on AWS, a big model you can run on your own computer inside Copilot, GIFs in ChatGPT Images, and Mistral offering to run your agents for you.
01RESEARCH BREAKTHROUGHPSI + ANTHROPICNOV 08, 2026

An AI Just Proved a Quantum Puzzle Unsolved for 18 Years

A startup called PSI said on November 6 that its research system, running a not-yet-public Anthropic model, proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture — a quantum computing question open since 2008. The system found a complete proof on day three, and Lean, a program that checks every single step, accepted it: 648 machine-checked theorems, no gaps left as placeholders. The paper and proof are public on GitHub, but no journal has reviewed it yet, so treat it as a strong, checkable claim — not a final verdict.

WHY IT MATTERSThis is AI doing original math at the frontier, with a proof anyone can re-check. It also sharpens a real question: quantum computers only get their huge speedups on problems with the right structure.
SOURCE →
02AGENT INFRASTRUCTUREGOOGLE + ANTHROPICNOV 08, 2026

AI Agents Can Finally Talk to Each Other — and They Stopped Making You Wait

Two quiet updates on November 7 that matter more than they sound. Google marked its Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol stable in ADK 2.14.0, which means agents built by different teams can now hand work to each other using one shared, finished standard. The same day, Claude Code 2.1.319 started running tool tasks in the background, so developers no longer sit and watch a spinner while it works.

WHY IT MATTERSAgents are only useful in teams. A stable shared language plus tools that work while you keep coding is how single chatbots turn into actual workflows.
SOURCE →
03OPEN SOURCENOUS RESEARCHNOV 08, 2026

This Open Model Was Retrained to Stop Repeating Propaganda

Nous Research released Arete-27B, a fine-tuned version of Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B, built to strip out one-sided state framing from its answers. On Nous's own test of 803 prompts, answers containing propaganda fell from 22% with the original model to 0.9%. The weights, the test, and the training data are all public, and the license is Apache 2.0, so anyone can check the claim or build on it.

WHY IT MATTERSEvery model carries the slant of its training data. This shows a small, open fix can measurably clean that up — and because everything is public, you don't have to take their word for it.
SOURCE →
04OPEN MODELSMOONSHOT AI + AWSNOV 08, 2026

A Huge Open Model Just Landed on AWS, Ready for Work

Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro is now available on Amazon Bedrock, AWS's managed AI service. Moonshot calls it its most capable model yet — an open-weight, multimodal model in the 3-trillion-parameter class, with a 1-million-token memory and a high-speed mode built for agent jobs like coding and document work. Those size and quality figures are Moonshot's own.

WHY IT MATTERSWhen a top open model shows up inside the cloud companies already pay for, with AWS security and controls around it, trying it stops being a research project and becomes a settings change.
SOURCE →
05RUN IT YOURSELFMICROSOFT + QWENNOV 08, 2026

You Can Now Run a Big AI Model on Your Own Computer, Inside Copilot

Microsoft showed how to run Qwen3.8-27B — a capable 27-billion-parameter open model — locally on your own GPU using its Foundry Local tool, and plug it straight into GitHub Copilot as the model behind your coding assistant. Your code stays on your machine, because the model does too.

WHY IT MATTERSLocal models used to mean clunky side projects. A one-setup path into the coding tool developers already live in makes private, no-cloud AI a real option for everyday work.
SOURCE →
06OPENAI CREATIVENOV 08, 2026

ChatGPT Images Can Now Make GIFs — and It Works 50% Faster

OpenAI rolled out ChatGPT Images 2.6 on November 4, and it is the version featured across this weekend's roundups for a reason: it can now generate looping GIFs and SVG files, keep the same character consistent across images using saved references, and handle denser text in pictures. OpenAI says it generates images about 50% faster than before — in some cases in as little as six seconds. Two developer versions, Flare and Sunburst, launched alongside it.

WHY IT MATTERSThis is the rare update you can play with today. Consistent characters plus quick animations turns image AI from one-off pictures into something you can actually build a series with.
SOURCE →
07MISTRAL ENTERPRISENOV 08, 2026

Mistral Will Now Run Your AI Agents for You

Mistral added managed agents to its Studio platform: instead of wiring up agent plumbing yourself, you get ready-made skills, safe sandboxes for agents to work in, and sub-agents that split up bigger jobs — and it can run on your own premises, not just Mistral's cloud. It is a preview, and the details come from Mistral's own announcement.

WHY IT MATTERSMost teams don't fail at picking a model; they fail at the boring infrastructure around agents. Renting that layer — especially on-prem, where sensitive data never leaves — removes the hardest part.
SOURCE →

REEL 01 · HIGHER-ED ANALYTICS · IPEDS

Retention Beats Wealth

Nine years of federal data, 8,670 colleges — Pell students finish at 45.9%, their classmates at 62.2%. The strongest predictor of finishing? First-year retention.

REEL 02 · HIGHER-ED ANALYTICS · IPEDS

Everyone Rose. The Gap Stayed.

Seven entering classes, 2009–2015 — Pell students climbed from 38.9% to 45.9%, their classmates from 54.4% to 62.2%. The gap between them: 15.5 points at the start, 16.4 at the end.

Watch on Instagram ↗ Watch on LinkedIn ↗ Watch on YouTube ↗ Full analysis (GitHub) ↗
REEL 03 · HIGHER-ED ANALYTICS · IPEDS

16.4 Is the Headline. 7.7 Is the Campus.

The famous Pell gap is 16.4 points — but that counts every student in the country, so the biggest institutions pull it up. Count campuses instead, one vote each, and the typical campus gap is 7.7 points. At 16% of campuses, Pell students actually finish ahead.

Watch on Instagram ↗ Watch on LinkedIn ↗ Watch on YouTube ↗ Full analysis (GitHub) ↗
REEL 04 · AI MODELS · REAL EXPERIMENT

Easy vs Hard

I gave ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini the same two problems. On the easy-looking one, two of them counted a duplicated row and answered 1,765 instead of 1,637. On the hard-looking one, all three pooled the totals correctly — 83.63%.

Watch on Instagram ↗
REEL 05 · CYBERSECURITY · DEEPMIND

Old Locks

DeepMind’s AI agents found two new weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA. One forgery attack now runs up to 1,600 times faster, and factoring extra keys in a batch costs about 30 times less. Modern encryption is fine — the risk is the old systems still running it.

Watch on Instagram ↗ Watch on LinkedIn ↗ Watch on YouTube ↗ Watch on Facebook ↗
REEL 06 · AI AT WORK · ROCKY PRESENTS

Go Nuts

Cisco handed one engineer an unlimited AI budget and told him: go nuts. His job is to refactor 98% of Cisco’s legacy code in two years, with a team of two — and he is 27. The honest part: 98% is a target, not a result; he gets four weeks to prove the method works. Rocky presents.
